defects.defective_behavior: When a defect has no named region, the review only reports a generic inability to mutate or a missing edit span, without stating that the defect is not editable for lack of a named region.

obligation_text: {"description":"A defect that names no region is not editable and is reported as such.","observable_behavior":"The review reports that a defect without a named region cannot be edited."}

defects.description: The validity check only parses Python-like files, so edited files with another parser can be accepted even when they no longer parse.
defects.expected_behavior: Every file type that has a parser in the mutation validity check is parsed after the edit, and malformed output for any such file is rejected.
defects.defective_behavior: Only `.py` and `.pyi` files are parsed, while other parseable file types are left to the non-parse checks and can pass validity even if they are syntactically broken.

defects.description: A parse failure from the mutated file is not rejected, so an invalid edit can still be treated as valid.
defects.expected_behavior: If the mutated file has a parser and parsing raises a syntax/value error, the edit is marked invalid.
defects.defective_behavior: If parsing raises a syntax/value error, the edit is still accepted as valid instead of being rejected.

obligation_text: {"description":"A file that has a parser still parses after the edit.","observable_behavior":"Parsing the file after the edit succeeds for files that have a parser."}

defects.description: Files without a parser are still treated as invalid, so the new validity check rejects them instead of allowing prose-only files to be mutated.
defects.expected_behavior: When a file has no parser, the validity check should skip the parse requirement and treat the file as valid on that ground.
defects.defective_behavior: When a file has no parser, the validity check reports the file invalid solely because no parser is available.

defects.description: The parse check only covers a fixed set of extensions, so a file type that does have a parser but is not listed can still be rejected or mishandled as if lacking one.
defects.expected_behavior: Any file type that has a parser should be treated as valid when its mutated text still parses under that parser.
defects.defective_behavior: Only the hardcoded extensions in the parser table are recognized, and other parseable file types are treated as outside the rule or invalid by omission.

defects.description: A malformed parse is converted into a generic not-mutable rejection, so the code can still be treating parser absence as an invalidity path instead of merely skipping the parse check for files that have no parser.
defects.expected_behavior: A file with no parser should pass validity on that ground alone, with parse-related rejection reserved for files that actually have a parser and fail it.
defects.defective_behavior: The validity path collapses parser-related cases into a not-mutable rejection, making parser absence function like a violation instead of a non-issue.

obligation_text: {"description":"A file with no parser is not invalid for lacking one.","observable_behavior":"The absence of a parser on a file is not treated as a violation of this requirement."}

defects.description: The new execution path can decide whether an edit is valid by running tests and halting or proceeding, so edit validity is no longer settled only by the mechanical validity checks.
defects.expected_behavior: Mechanical validity checks alone determine whether a mutation descriptor is valid, and execution settings only affect whether execution runs after validity is established.
defects.defective_behavior: The execution tier can short-circuit or override the validity decision by halting on baseline failures or proceeding past them, so validity depends on execution control flow as well as mechanical checks.

defects.description: The parse validity check only covers a small hardcoded set of suffixes, so files with another parser can be mutated without being checked for parse validity.
defects.expected_behavior: Any file type that has a parser must be re-parsed after the edit, so malformed mutants are rejected mechanically for every parseable file type the criterion covers.
defects.defective_behavior: Only .py, .pyi, and .json files are parsed after mutation, so other parseable file types can slip through validity checks even when the edit breaks them.

defects.description: The containment check only looks at regions that were resolved from the change set, so a defect with no resolved region can still be treated as mutable instead of being rejected mechanically.
defects.expected_behavior: If a defect names no editable region, mechanical validity rejects the edit as not mutable before any execution happens.
defects.defective_behavior: A defect with no resolved region can still reach later validity steps or be treated as valid because the containment check only runs after regions are found.

defects.description: A descriptor that declines by returning an empty region label is converted to None, but the runner still has to rely on later control flow to mark the defect not mutable, so the mechanical validity decision is not enforced at the descriptor boundary itself.
defects.expected_behavior: A declined descriptor is mechanically rejected as not mutable at the point the descriptor is interpreted, with no later stage able to treat it as a valid edit.
defects.defective_behavior: The descriptor builder can return None for a decline, and the runner separately turns that into not_mutable, leaving the validity decision unenforced at the descriptor stage.

obligation_text: {"description":"Whether an edit is valid is settled by mechanical checks alone.","observable_behavior":"Mechanical validation determines edit validity without human judgment."}

defects.description: The new execution tier can stop the review after the control run and remove failing candidate tests from later mutation and rating, so the set of tests treated as candidates is no longer the same as before.
defects.expected_behavior: The code that decides whether tests are candidates should remain unchanged by the new execution path; candidate selection should still be determined only by the existing discovery logic.
defects.defective_behavior: The code establishes a baseline run, halts on failing candidate tests unless overridden, and filters those tests out of later stages, changing which tests are treated as candidates.

defects.description: The new execution settings introduce a path that decides whether the review can run tests at all, instead of leaving that decision to the existing review flow.
defects.expected_behavior: The code should not add any new decision about whether the project's tests can be run at all; that decision should stay where it already was.
defects.defective_behavior: The pipeline now calls a baseline control run and can raise ReviewHalted when candidate tests fail at head, so the review itself decides whether tests may run.

obligation_text: {"description":"The change does not alter how the review decides whether a project's tests can be run at all or which tests are candidates.","observable_behavior":"The diff contains changes to the logic that determines whether tests can run at all or which tests are selected as candidates."}

defects.description: The review report or review state still includes a field or block that records executed line information, so the change continues to persist or render line execution data.
defects.expected_behavior: The delivered code should not store or display which lines of code a test executed anywhere in the review output or persisted review state.
defects.defective_behavior: The delivered code stores or renders line-execution information such as executed line spans, coverage line records, or a report section that lists executed lines.

defects.description: The new execution tier still feeds line-coverage-style evidence into support derivation, so the system continues to record which lines tests executed indirectly through evidence tier bookkeeping.
defects.expected_behavior: The delivered code should avoid recording executed lines as evidence and should only record test outcomes or mutation results relevant to the criterion.
defects.defective_behavior: The delivered code derives support from execution data that encodes line coverage or executed-line information, thereby preserving line-execution recording under a different name.

defects.description: The new execution path can still run the project's whole test suite because the runner is given the full discovered test list and there is no visible filter that limits execution to a named subset.
defects.expected_behavior: The execution tier should invoke only the named candidate tests, not the project's whole suite.
defects.defective_behavior: The execution tier passes the complete discovered test list into the sandbox runner, so the whole suite can be executed.

defects.description: The control run before mutation can execute every discovered test instead of only the named candidates, so the review may observe whole-suite execution before any defect injection happens.
